newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens stocks end 0.51pct lower in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Athens stocks end 0.51pct lower in profit-taking.

text.p: Greek equities ended down 0.51 percent on profit-taking and fund managers said they expected the bourse to stabilise in the next few sessions.

"The market is making a pause. This is natural, if one takes into account the fact that Wednesday's high, at 1,446.82, approached end-February's previous high of 1,453.60 points," said George Vendouratos, fund manager at Aspis Mutual Funds.
Some investors are getting nervous with the general index close to February's previous high, said Vendouratos.
"Investors will wait-to-see what happens for a few days. Some profit taking will take place and the market will probably stabilise by the end of this week," he said.
But all macroeconomic figures are positive and encouraging and will soon push the general share index up again, he added.

"I do not think that the drop in March's inflation to 6.0 percent year-on-year, from 6.6 percent in February, has been fully discounted by the bourse. I expect the market to react more favourably in the near future," he said.
With more news of easing inflation and interest rates, Vendouratos anticipates another rise in banking shares.

The Athens general share index closed 0.51 percent or 7.27 points lower at 1,429.28 from Tuesday's 1,436.55 close, after opening at 1,436.61. The session's high was at 1,446.82 and its low at 1,425.91 points.
Turnover dropped to 18.4 billion drachmas on volume of 4.1 million shares. Decliners led advancers 122 to 106, with 25 issues unchanged on 253 traded.
Sectoral indices were mixed. Banks lost 0.17 percent and construction fell 1.63 percent. Industrials dropped 0.94 percent, while leasing shares gained 0.46 percent.
Small caps ended down 0.39 percent and investment shares closed 0.15 percent lower.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted lower at 1,057.0-1,095.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were down 65 drachmas, to close at 6,415.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $58.41-$60.10. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 2,280-2,476 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
